findings.issue_text: Asymmetric subdomain detection: the case where the website is a subdomain of the instance host (with differing label counts) is never handled, causing inconsistent path display and arbitrary, direction-dependent truncation of the user's URL (e.g., website 'www.example.com' on instance 'example.com' silently drops the path)

Branch 1 of website_name uses exact string host comparison, so trailing-dot FQDNs (e.g., 'example.com.') don't match, fall through to branch 3, and the display name becomes the raw dotted host with no path

The client-side websiteName computed property was removed from user.js.es6 and only user.hbs was migrated to model.website_name; other templates/components binding websiteName may silently render empty bindings and should be confirmed against all templates referencing the user controller

Users with unparseable website URLs (spaces, unescaped characters, IDN hosts) cause URI() to raise, making website_name return nil and suppressing the entire globe/link block in the template — a user-visible regression versus the removed client-side split heuristic
Bare 'rescue nil' swallows all StandardError, not just URI parse failures, silently producing nil with no log trace and masking bugs — should be narrowed to URI::Error (or URI::InvalidURIError)

include_website_name returns website.present? but website_name can return nil for present websites (no-host URIs, parse failures), serializing inconsistent website_name: null alongside populated website — include condition should align with computed value

Sibling-subdomain match treats hosts with equal label counts and equal suffixes as 'same site' (e.g. forum.example.com vs www.example.com), producing false affiliation matches for unrelated sites under shared public suffixes like foo.co.uk vs bar.co.uk or a.github.io vs b.github.io, appending full path to displayed link text

The elsif branch of website_name (matching host-length domain logic with two outcomes) has zero test coverage; neither the suffix-match path (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) nor the non-match path (www.other.com vs forum.example.com) is exercised, so a regression like an off-by-one in split('.')[1..-1] would ship undetected

No edge-case tests for website URL formats the new URI-parsing logic must handle: scheme-less URLs (example.com/user), malformed URLs swallowed by rescue nil, ports (http://example.com:8080/x), https, and uppercase hosts are all untested; the no-scheme case interacts with include_website_name so the attribute may be emitted as nil

include_website_name conditional behavior is untested: there is no test asserting that website_name is omitted from the JSON when website is blank, so a regression in the attribute-inclusion contract would only surface as a rendering bug in production

Client-side behavior change (websiteName computed property deleted from user.js.es6 controller, template rebound to model.website_name) ships with no corresponding JS test; nothing verifies the template renders model.website_name or that the serializer actually serving the profile payload includes the attribute

Silent parse failure: URI() parse failures cause website_name to return null while include_website_name returns true, making the entire website link block disappear for unparseable URLs (non-ASCII/IDN hosts, unencoded spaces, malformed values) — a regression from the old client-side parsing, and an API inconsistency (include_website_name: true with null value)

Host comparisons are case-sensitive: none of the comparisons (equality, ends_with?, tail joins) downcase, so a user with http://Example.com/user against host example.com falls to the else branch and the feature silently doesn't apply

Complete URL path is not complete: only .path is appended, dropping query parameters, fragments, and port (e.g. ?page=2 omitted, :8080 port excluded), making the displayed text less accurate than the old title tooltip

Cascade risk: websiteName computed property removed from the controller but only templates/user/user.hbs updated; if any other template (e.g. user card) referenced websiteName it now silently renders nothing

Missing test coverage: the branch 2 logic (equal-length subdomain-tail comparison, www.example.com == forum.example.com, with the > 2 guard interaction) is never exercised in specs, leaving it vulnerable to regressions from issues 1 and 2

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Asymmetric subdomain detection: the case where the website is a subdomain of the instance host (with differing label counts) is never handled, causing inconsistent path display and arbitrary, direction-dependent truncation of the user's URL (e.g., website 'www.example.com' on instance 'example.com' silently drops the path)

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the “related domain” handling is asymmetric. The final `else` only includes the URL path when `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` (i.e., instance host is a subdomain of the website host, like `forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). It does not handle the inverse where the website host is a subdomain of the instance host (e.g., website `www.example.com` with instance `example.com`): `example.com.ends_with?(".www.example.com")` is false, so it returns only `website_host` and drops `URI(...).path`, matching the reported truncation/inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Branch 1 of website_name uses exact string host comparison, so trailing-dot FQDNs (e.g., 'example.com.') don't match, fall through to branch 3, and the display name becomes the raw dotted host with no path

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, branch 1 uses `website_host == discourse_host` with no normalization. If `URI(...).host` returns a trailing-dot FQDN like `example.com.`, it won’t match `Discourse.current_hostname` (`example.com`), so it falls through to later branches. In branch 3, `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` will also fail because `website_host` already includes the trailing dot, and the method returns `website_host` (no path), yielding a display like `example.com.` instead of including `/user` as intended for “same site/parent site” cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The client-side websiteName computed property was removed from user.js.es6 and only user.hbs was migrated to model.website_name; other templates/components binding websiteName may silently render empty bindings and should be confirmed against all templates referencing the user controller

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `websiteName` computed property from `controllers/user.js.es6` and updates `templates/user/user.hbs` to use `model.website_name`, but the claim that "other templates/components binding websiteName" will now render empty cannot be verified from the provided diff because no other template/component references are shown. The only shown consumer (`user/user.hbs`) was migrated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Users with unparseable website URLs (spaces, unescaped characters, IDN hosts) cause URI() to raise, making website_name return nil and suppressing the entire globe/link block in the template — a user-visible regression versus the removed client-side split heuristic

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves `websiteName` from a client-side `split("/")[2]` heuristic to a server-side `website_name` computed via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` (user_serializer.rb). If `URI()` raises for an invalid/unescaped website string, `website_host` becomes nil and `website_name` returns nil. The template now guards on `{{#if model.website_name}}` (user.hbs), so the globe/link block is suppressed even when `model.website` is present, changing visible behavior vs the removed client-side string split which would often still display something for malformed URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bare 'rescue nil' swallows all StandardError, not just URI parse failures, silently producing nil with no log trace and masking bugs — should be narrowed to URI::Error (or URI::InvalidURIError)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb`, the new `website_name` method uses `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`, which is a bare rescue that will catch any `StandardError` raised by that expression (not just invalid URI parsing). This can silently turn unexpected failures into `nil` without visibility, potentially masking bugs in the serializer logic. Narrowing the rescue to `URI::InvalidURIError`/`URI::Error` (or handling parse errors explicitly) would be safer.

adjudication_records.issue_text: include_website_name returns website.present? but website_name can return nil for present websites (no-host URIs, parse failures), serializing inconsistent website_name: null alongside populated website — include condition should align with computed value

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer`, `include_website_name` returns `website.present?`, but `website_name` can still return `nil` when `URI(website.to_s).host` is `nil` or parsing fails (`rescue nil` then `return if website_host.nil?`). That means the serializer can emit `website_name: null` while `website` is populated, which is inconsistent and suggests the include guard should align with the computed value (e.g., only include when `website_name` is non-nil). This is an edge-case/output-quality issue rather than a clearly broken behavior shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Sibling-subdomain match treats hosts with equal label counts and equal suffixes as 'same site' (e.g. forum.example.com vs www.example.com), producing false affiliation matches for unrelated sites under shared public suffixes like foo.co.uk vs bar.co.uk or a.github.io vs b.github.io, appending full path to displayed link text

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the “sibling subdomain” branch treats two hosts with the same label count (>2) as affiliated if everything after the first label matches: `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.')`. This will consider `foo.co.uk` and `bar.co.uk` (suffix `co.uk`) or `a.github.io` and `b.github.io` (suffix `github.io`) as “same site” and return `website_host + URI(...).path`, i.e., appending the full path to the displayed `website_name` even though the sites are unrelated. This behavior is directly introduced by the new serializer logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The elsif branch of website_name (matching host-length domain logic with two outcomes) has zero test coverage; neither the suffix-match path (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) nor the non-match path (www.other.com vs forum.example.com) is exercised, so a regression like an off-by-one in split('.')[1..-1] would ship undetected

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` branch (intended for cases like `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) is not exercised by the added specs. The specs cover: (1) different unrelated domains (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`) hitting the final `else`, (2) exact match (`example.com`), and (3) subdomain instance (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`) hitting the final `else` suffix check. None of the tests set both hosts to the same dot-length > 2, so neither outcome of the ternary inside that `elsif` (match vs non-match on `[1..-1]`) is covered, making regressions in that logic undetected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No edge-case tests for website URL formats the new URI-parsing logic must handle: scheme-less URLs (example.com/user), malformed URLs swallowed by rescue nil, ports (http://example.com:8080/x), https, and uppercase hosts are all untested; the no-scheme case interacts with include_website_name so the attribute may be emitted as nil

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial URI-based parsing in `UserSerializer#website_name` (`URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` plus hostname/path logic) and only adds specs for a single well-formed `http://example.com/user` input and a few hostname-comparison cases. It does not test scheme-less URLs, malformed URLs that hit the `rescue nil`, ports, https, or host canonicalization (e.g., uppercase). Also, `include_website_name` checks only `website.present?`, so inputs where `website` is present but `URI(...).host` is nil (e.g., scheme-less/relative) could result in the attribute being included but computed as nil—this interaction is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: include_website_name conditional behavior is untested: there is no test asserting that website_name is omitted from the JSON when website is blank, so a regression in the attribute-inclusion contract would only surface as a rendering bug in production

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `include_website_name` in `user_serializer.rb` to only include `website_name` when `website.present?`. The added spec coverage only exercises the "with filled out website" context and asserts values of `json[:website_name]`, but there is no test case where `user.user_profile.website` is blank/nil asserting that `website_name` is omitted from the serialized JSON. So the inclusion contract for the new conditional attribute is indeed untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side behavior change (websiteName computed property deleted from user.js.es6 controller, template rebound to model.website_name) ships with no corresponding JS test; nothing verifies the template renders model.website_name or that the serializer actually serving the profile payload includes the attribute

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* add coverage that the profile payload includes `website_name`: `user_serializer.rb` adds `:website_name` plus `include_website_name`, and `spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb` adds multiple expectations for `json[:website_name]`. The finding’s claim that “nothing verifies … the serializer … includes the attribute” is therefore contradicted by the diff. The separate point about missing JS/template tests is not verifiable from this diff alone (absence of added JS tests here doesn’t prove none exist).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent parse failure: URI() parse failures cause website_name to return null while include_website_name returns true, making the entire website link block disappear for unparseable URLs (non-ASCII/IDN hosts, unencoded spaces, malformed values) — a regression from the old client-side parsing, and an API inconsistency (include_website_name: true with null value)

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` will return `nil` on `URI` parse errors, and the method then `return if website_host.nil?`. However `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?`, so a present-but-unparseable `website` will still try to include `website_name` but yield `nil`. On the client, the profile template was changed to gate the entire website display on `{{#if model.website_name}}` (instead of deriving a name from `model.website`), so `website` can be present while the website link block disappears when parsing fails—behavior introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host comparisons are case-sensitive: none of the comparisons (equality, ends_with?, tail joins) downcase, so a user with http://Example.com/user against host example.com falls to the else branch and the feature silently doesn't apply

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, comparisons like `website_host == discourse_host`, the subdomain-tail equality, and `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` are all done without normalizing case. Since DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, if `URI(website.to_s).host` yields a differently-cased string than `Discourse.current_hostname`, the logic can take the wrong branch and omit the intended `+ path` behavior (or otherwise miscompute `website_name`). The diff shows no `downcase`/normalization on either value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Complete URL path is not complete: only .path is appended, dropping query parameters, fragments, and port (e.g. ?page=2 omitted, :8080 port excluded), making the displayed text less accurate than the old title tooltip

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the display string is built from `URI(website.to_s).host` and sometimes `+ URI(website.to_s).path`, which necessarily drops other URL components like query (`?x=1`), fragment (`#a`), and port (`:8080`, since `uri.host` excludes port). This affects the newly introduced `model.website_name` shown as link text in `user.hbs`. It’s a real edge-case/accuracy concern in the new logic, but the diff suggests `website_name` is intended as a simplified display name rather than a full URL, so it’s not clearly a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cascade risk: websiteName computed property removed from the controller but only templates/user/user.hbs updated; if any other template (e.g. user card) referenced websiteName it now silently renders nothing

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `websiteName` computed property from `controllers/user.js.es6` and updates `templates/user/user.hbs` to use `model.website_name`, but the claim that “any other template (e.g. user card) referenced websiteName” is not verifiable from the provided diff. No other templates are shown still referencing `websiteName`, and the finding is framed as a hypothetical (“if any other template…”), so it’s speculative rather than a diff-grounded defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test coverage: the branch 2 logic (equal-length subdomain-tail comparison, www.example.com == forum.example.com, with the > 2 guard interaction) is never exercised in specs, leaving it vulnerable to regressions from issues 1 and 2

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` method in `user_serializer.rb` has a distinct `elsif` branch for the case where `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and `> 2` (intended for scenarios like `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`). The added specs cover: different domains with 2-part hosts (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`, which skips the branch due to the `> 2` guard), exact host match (`example.com`), and parent-domain relation (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`, which hits the final `else`). None exercise the equal-length, >2 branch, so that logic is currently untested and could regress without detection.
